predecessors.name: New Kingdom of Egypt
predecessors.text: Egypt's Nubian province from the first cataract to Napata, independent 'with the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC'

successors.name: Nobatia
successors.text: Lower Nubia (Cliopatria's Nobatia shape); the Blemmyes 'in around 394 established a kingdom centered around Talmis' in its northern part

successors.name: Makuria
successors.text: the Dongola reach from the third cataract to Abu Hamed

successors.name: Alodia
successors.text: Meroë and the Gezira: 'Meroë was then taken by the Kingdom of Alodia' (Meroë page)

successors.name: Blemmyes
successors.text: the Dodekaschoinos and Talmis (Kalabsha): the Blemmyes 'in around 394 established a kingdom centered around Talmis'

ledger.x: c. 1000 BC: Kush emerges at Napata. 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC, Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata'; 'a Kushite kingdom began to emerge around 1000 BC'; the first named king, Alara, is dated 800-760 BC and the infobox gives 'Established: c. 780 BC'. The year is…

c. 591 BC: the capital moves to Meroë. 'Aspelta moved the capital to Meroë... possibly c. 591 BC', 'just after the sack of Napata by Psamtik II'; the Napata page: 'In 593 BC, it was sacked by the Egyptians and the Kushite capital was relocated to Meroë', and 'An Achaemenid…
274 BC: Ptolemy II takes Lower Nubia.

c. 204 BC: Kush retakes Lower Nubia. The Kush page: 'there was a serious revolt at the end of the reign of Ptolemy IV, around 204 BC'; 'Dynastic struggles led to the Ptolemies abandoning the area'; 'the Kushites reasserted their control' 'with Qasr Ibrim occupied' (the page does not give the year of the recovery…
22 BC: peace between Rome and Meroë.
22 BC: the frontier fixed at Hiera Sykaminos.
298: Kush takes the Dodekaschoinos after Rome leaves it.
331: the Aksumites leave Meroë ('for a short period of time'; the end is undated, one year is the researcher's).

wars.name: Kushite conquest of Egypt (Piye and Shabataka)
wars.outcome: Piye 'seized control of Lower Egypt around 727 BC' (campaigns 728-716 BC on the Victory Stela); Shabataka 'defeated the Saite kings of northern Egypt between 711 and 710 BC'; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty ruled Egypt from Memphis.

wars.name: Assyrian conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory (infobox 'Assyrian victory', 'The Neo-Assyrian Empire vassalised Egypt for a period of about 10 years'): Memphis taken 671, retaken by Taharqa 669, lost 667; Tantamani's recovery after 664 ended at Memphis and Thebes in 663; Upper Egypt…

wars.name: Psamtik II's Nubian campaign
wars.outcome: Napata sacked ('In 593 BC, it was sacked by the Egyptians'; Kush page: 'the sack of Napata by Psamtik II'); the capital moved to Meroë c.

wars.name: Ptolemy II's Nubian campaign
wars.outcome: 'In 275 or 274 BC, Ptolemy II ... sent an army to Nubia, and defeated the Kingdom of Kush'; the Triakontaschoinos 'was annexed to Egypt'.

wars.name: Roman-Kushite war (Petronius)
wars.outcome: Petronius 'invaded Nubia in 23 BC' and 'sacked Napata in 22 BC'; the Kushites attacked Qasr Ibrim in 22 BC; a peace 'under Augustus and Amanirenas, was signed in 22 BC' (Meroë page) and the border 'was moved to Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa)', guaranteeing…

wars.name: Aksumite campaigns against Meroë
wars.outcome: Aksum 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time' (Aksum page); an expedition 'after 340' followed the Atbara (Kush page); 'In 350 AD Meroë was destroyed by Axum' (Meroë page); the kingdom ended in the mid-4th century and Meroë 'was then…

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate; in Egypt (754-656 BC) the Kushite kings ruled through the existing nomes, so the Egyptian coast and desert edges follow Egypt's; the Nubian frontier with Ptolemaic Egypt after -274 is the second cataract, a…
The Roman frontier at Hiera Sykaminos (Maharraqa) is a treaty line from 22 BC and is the one sharp border; the Butana, Bayuda and Red Sea Hills frontiers stay soft.
